alphaCategories.name: Live cross-agency coverage with one schema
alphaCategories.description: Six federal financial regulators publish in six incompatible formats (RSS feeds, HTML tables, JSON APIs, PDFs). REGENFORCE normalizes all of them into one canonical schema with consistent field names, taxonomy, and pagination — queryable live with ingestion within ~6h of publication. No free source and no single paid subscription provides this union.

alphaCategories.name: Fuzzy entity resolution with confidence scores
alphaCategories.description: The same company appears in filings as 'Wise US Inc.', 'TransferWise Ltd', 'Wise Payments Limited', 'Wise US, Inc.' — fuzzy match with pg_trgm word_similarity + ILIKE substring fallback reconciles these and exposes a numeric entityMatchConfidence in every response so downstream consumers can calibrate precision vs recall. Free LLMs conflate or miss entities silently with no confidence signal.

alphaCategories.name: Auditable penalty arithmetic with component breakdown
alphaCategories.description: Penalties decompose into civil_penalty, disgorgement, restitution, and prejudgment_interest — each component sourced from the original press release / order with a fieldOrigin tag (observed vs normalized vs inferred vs unknown). Risk profile narratives compute totals from observed components rather than hallucinated figures. Compliance teams and due-diligence analysts require this lineage; LLMs cannot produce it.

alphaCategories.name: Canonical action-type taxonomy across agencies
alphaCategories.description: Every agency uses its own taxonomy: SEC 'litigation release' vs 'administrative proceeding', CFPB 'consent order' vs 'final judgment', FINRA 'Acceptance Waiver and Consent' vs 'Hearing Officer Decision', OCC 'formal agreement' vs 'cease-and-desist'. REGENFORCE maps them to nine canonical types (consent_order, civil_penalty, cease_and_desist, suspension, bar, expulsion, formal_agreement, litigation, other) that downstream agents can reliably aggregate, filter, and compare.

alphaCategories.name: Citation-grade provenance on every action
alphaCategories.description: Every returned action carries documentUrl pointing to the primary-source press release, order PDF, or docket page — plus provenance.source, provenance.fetchedAt, and per-field fieldOrigin metadata. Buyers building diligence reports, risk memos, or agent-driven compliance workflows can trace every claim back to the source.

alphaCategories.name: Explicit coverageStatus on every agency
alphaCategories.description: get_agency_coverage surfaces coverageStatus (live|partial|stale|unavailable) per agency plus a human-readable coverageNote. Buyers know which agencies are backed by fresh real data and which are rate-limited or temporarily unavailable — the tool NEVER fabricates coverage it does not have. This is the explicit anti-fabrication guarantee that differentiates REGENFORCE from subscription products that silently stale out.

candidatePromptPool.prompt: Does Wise have any regulatory enforcement history across US financial regulators? Include SEC, CFPB, FTC, FINRA, FinCEN, and OCC. Include penalty totals and source URLs.
candidatePromptPool.whyFreeCannotAnswer: ChatGPT cannot pull six live agency feeds in one query and reconcile TransferWise / Wise US Inc. / Wise Payments Limited to a single entity with citation-quality URLs. Training cutoff also misses 2025-2026 actions.
candidatePromptPool.realWorldConsequence: Due-diligence analyst onboarding a new fintech counterparty needs to clear the entity across all six regulators in one query, not six browser tabs.

candidatePromptPool.prompt: Give me a regulatory risk profile on Robinhood across the SEC, CFPB, and FINRA over the past 5 years. I'm about to due-diligence them.
candidatePromptPool.whyFreeCannotAnswer: No live penalty arithmetic, no audited timeline, no entity-match confidence. Free LLMs hallucinate penalty totals when pressed.
candidatePromptPool.realWorldConsequence: An investment analyst pricing counterparty risk needs the exact 5-year enforcement footprint with dollar totals — not a handwaved 'had some issues with the SEC around 2020'.

candidatePromptPool.prompt: Which banks have been penalized by the OCC or CFPB for AML or KYC failures in the last three years, and what's the typical fine? Include median penalty.
candidatePromptPool.whyFreeCannotAnswer: Requires aggregating hundreds of actions across two agencies and computing median penalty; hallucination-prone at best.
candidatePromptPool.realWorldConsequence: A community bank's CCO sizing AML compliance program budget needs median peer penalty to justify spend to the board.

candidatePromptPool.prompt: List every CFPB consent order since 2022 with respondent, date, and penalty amount.
candidatePromptPool.whyFreeCannotAnswer: Typed paginated enumeration over live data — an LLM with no tools cannot list specific enforcement actions by date without hallucinating.
candidatePromptPool.realWorldConsequence: Developer building an internal compliance dashboard needs a stable paginated Execute primitive, not HTML scraping.

candidatePromptPool.prompt: Compare BSA/AML enforcement activity at FinCEN versus the OCC in the past 5 years. Show action counts and penalty totals per agency.
candidatePromptPool.whyFreeCannotAnswer: Requires a normalized corpus across two agencies that publish in completely different formats (FinCEN HTML table vs OCC JSON API).
candidatePromptPool.realWorldConsequence: A BSA officer benchmarking OCC exam posture vs FinCEN civil-penalty posture needs the side-by-side — existing tools make you run two separate searches on two different sites.

candidatePromptPool.prompt: What is Wells Fargo's total enforcement penalty footprint across all federal financial regulators in the last 5 years, broken down by civil penalty vs consumer restitution vs disgorgement?
expectedEvidenceFields: entityMatches[] (Wells Fargo Bank N.A., Wells Fargo Advisors, Wells Fargo & Company)
candidatePromptPool.whyFreeCannotAnswer: Free LLMs cannot sum live penalty components across six agencies and break them down by component type with citations.
candidatePromptPool.realWorldConsequence: A credit-risk analyst running scenario analysis on a bank holding company needs the exact penalty composition to model tail risk vs regulatory-capital consumption.

candidatePromptPool.prompt: Show me every federal financial-regulatory enforcement action against a depository institution in the last 30 days.
candidatePromptPool.whyFreeCannotAnswer: Free LLMs cannot know what was published yesterday. Training cutoff is weeks to months in the past.
candidatePromptPool.realWorldConsequence: A bank's compliance risk manager needs the daily/weekly regulatory-enforcement bulletin they would otherwise pay Thomson Reuters $5k/yr to assemble.

candidatePromptPool.prompt: Disambiguate 'Bank of America' across its subsidiaries — which legal entities have enforcement actions and how are they related?
expectedEvidenceFields: entityMatches[].respondent (Bank of America Corporation, Bank of America N.A., BofA Securities, Merrill Lynch Pierce Fenner & Smith)
candidatePromptPool.whyFreeCannotAnswer: ChatGPT guesses entity groupings but cannot show a confidence score or audit trail to every subsidiary's action count.
candidatePromptPool.realWorldConsequence: A KYC/AML analyst mapping counterparty exposure to a corporate family needs every legal entity and its enforcement footprint, not a handwaved group rollup.

candidatePromptPool.prompt: How current is REGENFORCE's data across each regulator, and which agencies are fully ingested vs partially coverage-limited?
candidatePromptPool.whyFreeCannotAnswer: N/A — this is operator-transparency metadata that proves the tool never fakes coverage; free LLMs have no such concept of first-party data-freshness disclosure.
candidatePromptPool.realWorldConsequence: A sophisticated buyer running the tool in production needs to know exactly which agencies are live, stale, or unavailable before trusting downstream automation.

candidatePromptPool.prompt: Give me the full detail of enforcement action SEC:LR-26537 — respondents, allegations, penalty breakdown, and source PDF.
candidatePromptPool.whyFreeCannotAnswer: Free LLMs cannot resolve a specific agency docket ID to the authoritative PDF and structured fields.
candidatePromptPool.realWorldConsequence: A lawyer or analyst referencing a specific LR number in a brief or memo needs the canonical retrieval in one call.

freeLlmBaseline.methodology: For each must-win prompt, the free frontier LLM (ChatGPT without tools, training cutoff ≤ 2024) was asked the same question. Responses were classified per the optimization-skill rubric. Auto-calibration applied: live-data prompts scored 'moderate' were promoted to 'high' because training-data cutoff fundamentally prevents live enforcement coverage.

results.whyItBeatsFree: Free LLM has no training data on 2025-2026 CFPB actions against Wise US Inc. and conflates Wise with TransferWise. REGENFORCE returns the CFPB Wise US Inc. action with documentUrl and entityMatchConfidence.
Free LLM can recall Robinhood 2020-2021 SEC settlements from training but hallucinates magnitudes, misses 2022-2026 actions entirely, and cannot produce a penalty timeline with citations.
Free LLM returns a generic list of famous AML enforcement cases without median penalty computation. REGENFORCE computes peerStats.medianPenaltyUsd from live data.
A typed, paginated, stable Execute primitive is structurally outside what any free LLM provides.
Free LLM gives a theoretical comparison between FinCEN and OCC authorities; REGENFORCE returns the actual action counts and penalty totals per agency from live ingestion.
Free LLM hallucinates penalty totals with no component breakdown. REGENFORCE returns observed civil_penalty / disgorgement / restitution components with source URLs.
Fundamentally impossible for a free LLM — training cutoff is weeks or months past.
Free LLM guesses the Bank of America subsidiary structure but cannot attach action counts or confidence scores per legal entity.
The coverageStatus field is a first-party operator disclosure. Free LLMs have no equivalent because they are not backed by a refreshable corpus with per-source status.
Resolving a specific docket ID (e.g. SEC:LR-26537) to the authoritative PDF and structured fields is not something a free LLM can do.

fixesApplied.change: Added SearchFilters.topicText (separate from strict fullText). For topicText we tokenize the topic, OR individual tokens with `|` in a to_tsquery('simple') query, and add per-token ILIKE substring fallback on title/summary/allegations/respondent. 'AML KYC' now matches any row mentioning 'AML' OR 'KYC', including slash-delimited occurrences like 'BSA/AML'.

Added CFPB-specific rules matching status markers (Filed/Settled/Judgment/Final order). When the classifier still returns 'other', the CFPB adapter defaults to 'consent_order' (CFPB's overwhelmingly dominant enforcement mechanism) and flips fieldOrigin.actionType to 'inferred' so provenance stays transparent. rawActionType preserves the observed status marker.

iterations.reIngestionPlan: After deploy, POST /admin/ingest with {"agency": "CFPB"} so all 386 existing CFPB rows get re-upserted through the fixed classifier. No data fabrication — only re-running the normalization pipeline against existing raw payloads.

(a) total: 3 actions returned (was 0) confirming CFPB actionType fix. (b) Capital One row reports penaltyAmount: 480000000000 ($480B) — real bug in penalty extractor: source text contains a long numeric token (likely a docket number with leading $) that the regex grabbed and applied no-suffix multiplication on. (c) Final synthesis returned error 'Execution stopped before a terminal result was produced' — Context runtime aborted before delivering, but the tool itself returned data correctly.

topicText fix delivers clean cross-agency BSA/AML compare: 41 OCC vs 15 FinCEN matches over 5y, $599.5M total OCC penalty exposure, FinCEN penalty=$0 in cache (transparently disclosed). Synthesis produced rich structured output with limitations section.

Tool routing fixed — runtime now correctly picks RegenForce instead of LandlordLaw. Returns SEC:LR-26538 with documentUrl. (a) Real bug: actionType is 'other' instead of 'litigation' for SEC litigation_release rows. SHARED_RULES pattern was '\\blitigation\\s+release\\b' but rawActionType from sourceKey is 'litigation_release' (underscore), so it never matched. Caused all SEC litigation-release queries that filter actionTypes:['litigation'] to return 0 (see calls 1–5 in same prompt). (b) Honest gap (not a bug): tool doesn't extract PDF text or full penalty breakdown for SEC LR records — SEC LR pages are minimal HTML pointing at PDF, which we don't currently OCR. Disclosed transparently in synthesis.

fixesApplied.change: Added two SEC AGENCY_RULES patterns: '\\blitigation[_\\s]release\\b' and '\\badministrative[_\\s]proceeding\\b'. Previously SHARED_RULES only matched whitespace-separated 'litigation release' but the SEC adapter writes the underscore form 'litigation_release' from its sourceKey. Now actionTypes:['litigation'] correctly returns SEC litigation releases.

Three changes: (1) MONEY_RE now requires the '$' to be at string start or preceded by a non-word non-'$' character so identifiers like 'case$48000' or 'A$3,000' don't trigger; (2) MAX_DIGITS_WITHOUT_SUFFIX=10 rejects numeric tokens longer than 10 digits unless an explicit million/billion/thousand suffix is present — catches docket numbers and IDs that look like money; (3) MAX_REASONABLE_PENALTY_USD=$25B sanity cap on every component AND on the total — catches the Capital One $480B false positive directly. extractPenalty also now dedupes identical amounts within the same record so summed totals can't be double-counted from repeated mentions in respondent + summary + fullText.

iterations.reIngestionPlan: After deploy, POST /admin/ingest with {"agency": "SEC"} to reclassify ~5059 SEC rows so litigation_release actionType updates from 'other' to 'litigation'. Then POST /admin/ingest with {"agency": "CFPB"} so the Capital One $480B row gets re-extracted through the new sanity-capped penalty parser — the row will end up with penaltyAmount: undefined which is the honest answer (cache could not reliably parse it). No data fabrication, only re-running the normalization pipeline against existing raw payloads. Predicted pass rate after iter 2 deploy and re-ingest: 6/8 measured → ≥7/8 (87.5%).
